newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat says 1997 results not below 1996.
newsitem.headline: Fiat says 1997 results not below 1996.

text.p: Cesare Romiti, the chairman of Italy's industrial giant Fiat, said its results for 1997 will not be below those of 1996, without counting on the capital gains made in 1996.

In an interview with the Turin-based La Stampa newspaper Romiti said that for 1997: "I can forecast that we will eliminate debts, the financial position will be profit making and results will not be less than 1996 not counting the capital gains of last year," Romiti said.

Fiat showed a net consolidated profit in 1996 of 2.371 trillion lire from 2.147 trillion lire in 1995. In 1996, Fiat's profits gained from the partial flotation of its New Holland farm machinery arm and the sale of fund management group Prime to insurer Generali.
